Therefore[a], seeing them being scourged and harried like this, I was grieved for them, because they were being tormented in this way and had no respite at all. I said to the shepherd who was speaking with me, “Sir, who is this shepherd, so pitiless and harsh, showing no compassion at all for these sheep?” He said, “This is the angel of punishment; he is one of the righteous angels[b], appointed over punishment. Therefore he takes over those who have wandered away from God and have gone after the desires and deceits of this age, and he punishes them, as they deserve, with dreadful and various punishments.”

“I wished, Sir,” I said, “to know what these various punishments are.” He said, “Listen. The various punishments and torments are torments of this present life: for some are punished with losses, some with deprivations, some with various sicknesses, some with every kind of disorder; some are insulted by the unworthy, and suffer in many other undertakings. For many, being unsettled in their plans, take on many projects, and nothing at all advances for them. They say of themselves that they do not prosper in their undertakings, and it does not rise up into their heart that they have done evil, but they blame the Lord.

“When, then, they are pressed by every affliction, then they are handed over to me for good discipline, and they are strengthened in faith in the Lord; and the rest of the days of their life they serve the Lord with a pure heart. And if they repent[j], then the evil works that they did rise up into their heart; and then they glorify God, saying that he is a righteous judge and that each one suffered justly according to his deeds. Thereafter they serve the Lord with a pure heart, and they prosper in every work of theirs, receiving from the Lord whatever they ask for; and then they glorify the Lord because they were handed over to me[i][h][g][f][e][d][c], and they no longer suffer any of the evils.”

'Angel of punishment' could also be rendered 'angel of retribution.' The Greek τιμωρία denotes punitive justice.
'Torments of this present life' clarifies that βιωτικαί refers to temporal, not eschatological, afflictions.

'Strengthened in faith in the Lord' could also be taken as 'strengthened in the Lord’s faithfulness.' The context favors faith directed toward the Lord.
Or 'Seeing them being scourged'.

patches.old:
When I saw them being whipped and made to suffer like this, I was grieved for them. They were being tormented without any relief. I asked the shepherd who was speaking with me, “Sir, who is this shepherd? He is pitiless and harsh and shows these sheep no mercy.”

He answered, “This is the angel of punishment. He is one of the righteous angels appointed to carry out punishment. He takes charge of those who have wandered away from God and followed the desires and deceptions of this age. He punishes them as they deserve with many kinds of terrible punishments.”

“Sir,” I said, “I want to know what these different punishments are.”

He replied, “Listen. These different punishments and torments are sufferings in this present life. Some people lose what they have. Some are deprived of things. Some suffer from various diseases. Some suffer from every kind of trouble. Some are insulted by unworthy people, and some suffer in many other ways.

“Many cannot settle on what to do. They begin many things, but nothing succeeds for them. They say that none of their efforts prosper. It does not occur to them that they have done evil; instead, they blame the Lord.”

“After they have suffered every kind of affliction, they are handed over to me so that I may correct and train them. Their faith in the Lord grows stronger, and for the rest of their lives they serve him with pure hearts. When they repent[a], their evil deeds come back to mind. Then they glorify God and say that he judges rightly, and that each of them suffered justly for what they had done. From then on, they serve the Lord with pure hearts. They prosper in all they do and receive from the Lord whatever they ask. Then they glorify the Lord because they were handed over to me, and they no longer suffer any of those evils.”

So when I saw them being whipped[g] and made to suffer like this, I was grieved for them. They were being tormented without any relief. I asked the shepherd who was speaking with me[a], “Sir, who is this shepherd? He is so[k] pitiless and harsh and shows these sheep no mercy.”

He answered, “This is the angel of punishment[b]. He is one of the righteous angels. He is appointed to oversee punishment. So he takes charge of those[h] who have wandered away from God and followed the desires and deceptions of this age. He punishes them as they deserve with many kinds of terrible punishments.”

“Sir,” I said, “I want to know what these different punishments are.”

He replied, “Listen. These different punishments and torments are sufferings in this present life[c]. For some people are punished by losing what they have. Some are deprived of things. Some suffer from various diseases. Some suffer from every kind of[k] trouble. Some are insulted by unworthy people and suffer in many other undertakings[i].

“For many cannot settle on what to do. They begin many things[d], but nothing succeeds for them. They say that none of their efforts prosper. It does not occur to them[e] that they have done evil; instead, they blame the Lord.”

“When, then, they suffer every kind of affliction, they are handed over to me for good correction and training. Their faith in the Lord[f] grows stronger, and for the rest of their lives they serve him with pure hearts. But if they repent[j], then the evil deeds they did come to mind. Then they glorify God and say that he judges rightly, and that each of them suffered justly for what they had done. From then on, they serve the Lord with pure hearts. They prosper in all they do and receive from the Lord whatever they ask. Then they glorify the Lord because they were handed over to me, and they no longer suffer any of those evils.”
patches.reason: Independently restore singular appointment scope (κείμενος), the shared participant group and undertakings (ὑβριζόμενοι…πάσχοντες), conditional repentance (ἐὰν), good discipline (ἀγαθήν), and explicit reasoning links (οὖν, γάρ). Restore bracketed οὕτως without silently deleting it, disclose both bracketed words, and anchor every supplied note to its subject. Explicit punishment language also preserves τιμωροῦνται γάρ. Preserve all six paragraph divisions.
